sentences.text: Fossils of Psammodus are primarily known from their plate-like teeth, which were broad, flat, and often rectangular or triangular in shape. In life, these teeth were tightly packed together within the jaws.
The genus Psammodus was first described and named by the naturalist Louis Agassiz.

Psammodus were carnivores that ate hard-shelled prey. The tooth plates of Psammodus were specifically adapted for durophagy, the consumption of hard objects. They likely ate small benthic invertebrates with hard shells and occasionally small fish, similar to modern chimaeras.
Researchers suggest that Psammodus ground food between its upper and lower tooth plates instead of crushing it.
Psammodus is the only known member of the family Psammodontidae and the order Psammodontiformes. Psammodus serves as the type genus for both the family Psammodontidae and the order Psammodontiformes.

Psammodus lived during the Late Devonian to the Early Carboniferous periods. The time range for Psammodus is recorded from the Tournaisian to the Bathonian, between 358.86 and 165.3 million years ago.
